summary: Round 3 recheck (~22:15-22:45 UTC 25 Sep): three closed ideas that rounds 1-2 did not touch. Rounds 1-2 already covered floatout, I-077/I-078, tempfuse, RE-AIM/BYTE/pair-GBM, the 6bba extension, the runtime-rejected ideas and DNVETO with its probe-20 analogue. Two of the three were re-measured on CPU on the exp60 x138 lab (56 train clips, official metric, replay parity 56/56). (A) swapfix / 2x2 swap re-assignment (I-165/I-166) STAYS CLOSED. The old verdict said swaps are a node-position problem and the coordinate head is the fix. x138 has the head, yet the swap signature is unchanged. both_linked FN are 33% of lab FN (555/1,705). For them the GT link is 3.17 um, but its matched pred nodes are 9.13 um apart, our links are 1.5-1.6 um and the matches sit at 3.9/4.2 um. There are 0 true 2x2 swaps, and a geometric 2x2 rule finds 57 candidates on 56 clips with 1 new TP. (B) Clip-boundary frames / boundary-aware short-track filter (I-145, with I-129 as calibration) STAYS CLOSED. On x138 the deficit is real: GT node recall is 0.94-0.95 in the first and last 3 frames against 0.986 mid, and x138's own tail after presafe causes about half of it. A boundary rescue arm (add back removed chain components touching t0/T-1) gives +0.00056 pooled. But SELECTION is +0.00000, W/L is 7/47 clips, nodes rise +0.48% and one tiny 44b6 clip carries it (+0.00033 without that clip). That fails the old pre-registered bar (>= +0.001, nodes <= +0.4%, 55% wins). The same lab rates global MIN_TRACK_LEN 4 at +0.00015, where the LB said -0.002 (probe 6), so the lab over-rates keeping short components. The rule is also a node-set changer, so it needs R4's +0.002 public, and R8 applies. (C) Axis-flip TTA group (I-151), re-read under 'public = one embryo, private = other embryos' and the ~4 h headroom: STAYS CLOSED. The view count is unchanged, so the headroom is irrelevant. Its best evidence (+0.0187 on an unseen-embryo scratch primary) comes from the same control design that gave Z-flip +0.0098 before Z-flip lost 0.009 on the LB. The public -0.001 is a real test-embryo read, and on x138 the change would shift detections, readmit/lowdet, the head, DaughterNet inputs and every dummy calibration, with no honest lab. None of the three revives, and no plan change follows. The only new, reusable fact is the lab calibration point: node-count arms on exp60 disagree in sign between SELECTION and CONFIRMATION and read ~+0.002 more favourable than the LB.

findings.what: swapfix / 2x2 swap re-assignment and multi-frame swap tests (I-165, I-166). OLD VERDICT (24 Sep, exp39 base): 'SWAPS ARE NOT LINKING ERRORS'. In swaps the GT link was 2.6 um, but its matched pred nodes were 9.4 um apart. Our links were short (~1.5 um), motion preferred ours in 98.6%, and endpoints matched GT at 4.4/4.7 um. --patch swapfix gave -0.00004 on CONFIRMATION (FAIL). Prescription: 'a NODE-POSITION problem: coordinate head (x138) ...'. WHAT CHANGED: x138 now carries exactly that fix (V1284 head, float coords, flow-prior relink). Round 1 (M1) found 41/82 x138 dummy FN are frag_both_linked but did not measure their geometry, so the premise was open on the new base. MEASURED NOW on exp60 (56 clips, control = kernel final graph, official 7 um DistanceMatching). GT edges 40,093; FN 1,705 = miss 834 (49%) / both_linked 555 (33%) / one_free 305 (18%) / both_free 11. both_linked medians: GT link 3.17 um, matched pred nodes 9.13 um apart (9.06 flow-compensated), current links 1.60/1.53 um, pred-to-GT match 3.91/4.20 um. True 2x2 swaps (pa->pd, pc->pb with GT c->d): 0 of 555. The GT-implied link is shorter than ours in 0.4% of cases. A 2x2 geometric rule over all single-child edge pairs (sources < 10 um, gain > 0.5 um, raw or flow-compensated) gives 51-57 candidates on 56 clips: 0 current TP destroyed and 1 new TP. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED, now with x138 evidence. The head did not turn swaps into linking errors. The residual both_linked FN are GT nuclei that sit ~4 um from two different pred tracks: localisation or over-segmentation that no linker rule can fix. They are reachable only by detector retraining (R9, after 29 Sep).

findings.what: Clip-boundary frames (I-145; ILP end exemption and a boundary-aware short-track filter), with global OUTPUT_MIN_TRACK_LEN (I-129) as calibration. OLD VERDICT (v2 Dropped, old base): 'no detector padding; the ILP end effect has a +0.0011 oracle, which the node multiplier cancels'. The tail-only rule was pre-registered at -0.0003..+0.0003 with a success bar of >= +0.001, nodes <= +0.4% and boundary FN down >= 25%. WHAT CHANGED: the x138 tail (readmit, gapfill, rescue logic) differs, the exp60 lab can now replay the short-track filter on CPU, and ranking inside a displayed-score block by the unrounded score makes +0.0003..+0.0005 matter. MEASURED on exp60. (1) The deficit persists on x138. GT node recall at presafe -> final: t0 0.959 -> 0.940, t1 0.968 -> 0.954, t2 0.967 -> 0.948, t-3 0.967 -> 0.959, t-2 0.966 -> 0.947, t-1 0.956 -> 0.951, mid 0.986 -> 0.986. Boundary edge TP rate is 0.926 vs 0.958 interior, so about half of the deficit comes from x138's own post-presafe tail. (2) Arm bK: after x138's filter_short_track_components, add back removed chain components of >= K nodes touching t0 or T-1 (replayed from the 'preshort' hook; control parity 56/56). b4: pooled +0.00056, SELECTION +0.00000, CONFIRMATION +0.00109, 44b6 +0.0034 / 6bba +0.0003, W/L 7/47 clips, nodes +0.48%. Over 56 clips: edge TP +25, FP -17, nodes +5,345. The single tiny clip 44b6_9be80b04 (w = 236) gives +0.042, and without it the pooled gain is +0.00033. b5: +0.00039 at nodes +0.26%. (3) Calibration on the same lab: global MIN_TRACK_LEN 4 = +0.00015 (nodes +2.13%, W/L 12/44, SEL -0.0007 / CONF +0.0010), 5 = +0.00002, 8 = -0.00023. The LB read of that lever was 4 = -0.002 (probe 6) and 8 = -0.001 (probe 9), on the older base. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED. The x138 lab confirms the deficit but not a usable rule: it fails the old pre-registered bar (win rate 13%, nodes above 0.4%, SELECTION 0), and the positive pooled number has the same outlier-driven shape as MIN_TRACK_LEN 4, which lost 0.002 on the LB. It is a node-set changer, so R4 needs +0.002 public (unreachable) and R8 ends new mechanisms at 27 Sep 12:00. The upstream half (presafe recall 0.956-0.968 at the ends) is the ILP end effect, which needs a pre-ILP candidate dump plus GPU: post-deadline only.

findings.what: Axis-flip TTA group (I-151 / B30 / A28): the 8 training-consistent axis flips replace the rot90/transpose views; the view count is unchanged. OLD VERDICT: local +0.0214 on 12 videos, +0.0187 on a scratch primary that never saw 44b6, raw nodes flat. LB probe 19 exp37 = 0.946 vs exp29 0.947: 'tie, closed as a gain'. v3 section i: 'axis-flip on x138 closed on LB, lab biased'. WHAT CHANGED: (1) The public LB is ONE test embryo (~29%) and the private LB is other embryos (71%), so a one-embryo tie against an unseen-embryo local gain could look like an embryo-specific miss. (2) The ~4 h runtime headroom removes any runtime objection. (3) The 'LB noise +-0.003' premise is overturned, so the -0.001 is a real public-embryo read. RE-READ: (a) The headroom is irrelevant, because the view count is unchanged and runtime was never the blocker. (b) The unseen-embryo control design has already failed once: in B26 Z-flip kept +0.0098 on the unseen-44b6 scratch primary and then scored -0.009 on the LB (probe 16). So '+0.0187 on an unseen-embryo primary' is not evidence of transfer to a new test embryo. The only test-embryo read of axis-flip is -0.001, and it is now known to be real. (c) On x138 a TTA-group change shifts raw detections and edge features. It therefore moves readmit/lowdet pools, the V1284 head gather, DaughterNet insertion inputs and every K2 dummy calibration (LOWDET counts, +-0.3% node gate), and exp60 is in-sample for the detector, so there is no honest lab. (d) It is a node/fork-set changer: R4 needs +0.002 public, the prior public read is -0.001, and R8 closes new mechanisms at 27 Sep 12:00. Its variance works against the finals objective P(private F1 > x138). NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED. The public/private split does not revive it, and the reason is sharpened: the unseen-embryo control was falsified by Z-flip, not merely 'the lab is biased'.
